chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Sindi ibn Muhammad, from al-Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: 'For the goods (merchandise) in which I do not make a profit to cover the principal capital, is Zakat obligatory upon me?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'If I keep them for two years and then sell them, what is due from me?' He said: 'One year.'

As for that which indicates that Zakat on commercial property is not obligatory (fard), but rather recommended (mandub mustahabb), is what we have previously mentioned: that Zakat is only obligatory on Rikaz (buried treasure), and on struck and hoarded Dirhams and Dinars, and for other than these, there is no Zakat.
And this is confirmed by what he narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zakat for commercial goods held for less than a year?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the hawl (lunar year) for commercial merchandise begins upon acquisition, not necessarily at a fixed calendar date, and Zakat is due upon sale or completion of the year. The text further elaborates on the jurisprudential debate regarding whether Zakat on trade goods is obligatory (wajib) or recommended (mustahabb), contrasting it with the clear obligation on hoarded gold and silver (kanz). This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly view that while Zakat on trade is highly emphasized, its status may differ from the primary categories of Zakat mentioned in the Quran.
